cust-rep: customer 9371 opening CS-1289 — intermittent 502/504s on hosted API since ~20:10 UTC. They report p95 tail timeouts around 5-7s, then gateway 504s. sample trace id trc_93a7
incidents-bot: alert fired > hosted-api.p95_tail > 5s for route /v1/generate (20:11 UTC)
alice: looking at gateway logs now. I can see a big queue buildup for tenant=acme-inc starting 20:08. queue_depth climbed to ~10k, continuous-batcher backlog rising.
ben: sharing a small log snippet from gateway/ingress:
```
[20:12:13] enqueue id=abc123 tenant=acme-inc queue_len=10234 batcher_pending=78
[20:12:14] dequeue id=abc123 wait=4.92s -> timeout -> 504
[20:12:15] enqueue id=def456 tenant=acme-inc queue_len=10310 batcher_pending=81
```
ingress-oncall: looks like a traffic shift from acme-inc spikeed thinpool usage and exceeded per-tenant queue cap. continuous batching increased head-of-line pressure; some requests never make it to GPU before request deadline.
support-bot: customer supplied repro curl and small payload: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"prompt":"short"}'` — they reported sending many concurrent small requests (concurrency ~1200) after a config roll.
dave: can we mitigate quickly? Options: 1) temporarily disable continuous batching for tenant, 2) route to smaller model variant, 3) bump per-tenant queue cap, or 4) shed aggressively with 429 to reduce enqueue pressure.
alice: applied mitigation step 1 — disabled batching for acme-inc via runtime flag: `rbctl set tenant acme-inc batching=off`. immediate effect: subset p95 dropped from ~5s -> ~420ms in ~30s for routed traffic. overall cluster still high but improving.
ben: added temporary routing fallback for heavy tenants to medium model (lower memory, faster throughput) — reduces thinpool saturation.
ingress-oncall: created ticket RINF-2367 to track permanent fixes: increase per-tenant queue_capacity, adaptive shedding, and autoscale thinpool pools on traffic shift. Also add a telemetry alert for batcher_pending > 50 for 1m.
alice: repro notes: to reproduce locally, send many small concurrent requests with that token, watch gateway enqueue metrics and `batcher_pending` gauge. sample command used in load test: `hey -n 20000 -c 1200 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
ben: suggested follow-ups for product: shorten default request deadline for hosted route (current 12s) and surface 429 clients when queue_depth > X to avoid tail 504s.
dave: outreach — cust-rep to update customer with temporary mitigations and ask them to throttle concurrent bursts while we implement long-term changes.
support-bot: ticket CS-1289 updated with mitigation steps + traces + runbook link https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/queue-surge
cust-rep: customer okay with temporary disable of batching and routing fallback; they want RCA and ETA on permanent fix. will keep them informed. :thumbsup:
ingress-oncall: we'll follow up in RINF-2367, owning timeline and postmortem; assigning to eng-runtime and eng-platform.
